title: 1 Samuel 4: The Ark of God Is Taken
body:
Read the chapter → [1 Samuel 4](/bible/1-samuel/4)

## Introduction

This session covers 1 Samuel chapters 4 through 7, the war between Israel and one of our main enemies in the Old Testament, the Philistines, and their weak fake god Dagon. Samson had already crushed Dagon's house down on the Philistines in the book of Judges, yet they rebuilt him, and the prophets keep having to humiliate their gods. Here Israel loses the ark of the covenant in battle, the Most High plagues the Philistines from city to city until they send it back, and the prophet Samuel rises up for the nation of Israel, showing that prayer is a spiritual power: when a righteous man sends up prayer, the Most High will come down in thunder against the enemies of his people. Reading about our forefathers being attacked by the other nations prepares us for the same persecution today; as the works increase, so does the attack, so stay girded up and stay focused.

**[1 Samuel 4:1-2](/bible/1-samuel/4#v1)**

> <sup>[1](/bible/1-samuel/4#v1)</sup> And the word of Samuel came to all Israel. Now Israel went out against the Philistines to battle, and pitched beside Eben–ezer: and the Philistines pitched in Aphek.
>
> <sup>[2](/bible/1-samuel/4#v2)</sup> And the Philistines put themselves in array against Israel: and when they joined battle, Israel was smitten before the Philistines: and they slew of the army in the field about four thousand men.

- The word of Samuel came to all Israel, and Israel went out against the Philistines to battle, pitching beside Ebenezer while the Philistines pitched in Aphek. The Philistines never wanted to leave Israel alone.
- When they joined battle, Israel was smitten before the Philistines, and about four thousand men of the army fell in the field. The Philistines came up against us and whooped us in this first battle.

**[1 Samuel 4:3-5](/bible/1-samuel/4#v3)**

> <sup>[3](/bible/1-samuel/4#v3)</sup> And when the people were come into the camp, the elders of Israel said, Wherefore hath the Lord smitten us to day before the Philistines? Let us fetch the ark of the covenant of the Lord out of Shiloh unto us, that, when it cometh among us, it may save us out of the hand of our enemies.
>
> <sup>[4](/bible/1-samuel/4#v4)</sup> So the people sent to Shiloh, that they might bring from thence the ark of the covenant of the Lord of hosts, which dwelleth between the cherubims: and the two sons of Eli, Hophni and Phinehas, were there with the ark of the covenant of God.
>
> <sup>[5](/bible/1-samuel/4#v5)</sup> And when the ark of the covenant of the Lord came into the camp, all Israel shouted with a great shout, so that the earth rang again.

- The elders of Israel asked the right question, Wherefore hath the Lord smitten us to day before the Philistines? But instead of examining the nation, they had an idea: fetch the ark of the covenant out of Shiloh, and when it comes among us it will save us out of the hand of our enemies.
- The two sons of Eli, Hophni and Phinehas, came with the ark, and when it entered the camp all Israel shouted with a great shout so that the earth rang again. That is how excited and ecstatic Israel was to have the ark of the covenant among them; they felt their enemies could not destroy them now.
- So what is the ark of the covenant, and what does it contain? The Lord told Moses to hew two tables of stone like the first ones he broke, and the Lord rewrote the ten commandments on them with his own finger, and Moses put the tables in the ark. The ark of the covenant contained the commandments that God wrote.

  Precepts:
  - **[Deuteronomy 10:1-2](/bible/deuteronomy/10#v1)**
    > <sup>[1](/bible/deuteronomy/10#v1)</sup> At that time the Lord said unto me, Hew thee two tables of stone like unto the first, and come up unto me into the mount, and make thee an ark of wood.
    >
    > <sup>[2](/bible/deuteronomy/10#v2)</sup> And I will write on the tables the words that were in the first tables which thou brakest, and thou shalt put them in the ark.

    The Lord instructed Moses to hew two tables of stone like unto the first, make an ark of wood, and put in it the tables the Lord would write on.
  - **[Exodus 32:19](/bible/exodus/32#v19)**
    > <sup>[19](/bible/exodus/32#v19)</sup> And it came to pass, as soon as he came nigh unto the camp, that he saw the calf, and the dancing: and Moses’ anger waxed hot, and he cast the tables out of his hands, and brake them beneath the mount.

    Moses broke the first tables when he came down from the mount and saw the people dancing before the golden calf they had made from their gold earrings.
  - **[Deuteronomy 10:3-5](/bible/deuteronomy/10#v3)**
    > <sup>[3](/bible/deuteronomy/10#v3)</sup> And I made an ark of shittim wood, and hewed two tables of stone like unto the first, and went up into the mount, having the two tables in mine hand.
    >
    > <sup>[4](/bible/deuteronomy/10#v4)</sup> And he wrote on the tables, according to the first writing, the ten commandments, which the Lord spake unto you in the mount out of the midst of the fire in the day of the assembly: and the Lord gave them unto me.
    >
    > <sup>[5](/bible/deuteronomy/10#v5)</sup> And I turned myself and came down from the mount, and put the tables in the ark which I had made; and there they be, as the Lord commanded me.

    Moses made an ark of shittim wood, the Lord wrote on the tables the ten commandments he spake out of the midst of the fire, and Moses put the tables in the ark, and there they be.

- The law is spiritual, and the law has literal spiritual power; the commandments have always been our source of power as a nation. The church teaches that the laws are done away with, but watch in these chapters how seriously the Lord regarded the ark that contained his commandments.
- Watch also why the ark did not have the effect Israel expected in this battle: there were still Israelites in the midst of idolatry with idols among them, and until those idols were put away we could not be delivered from our enemies. That is the lesson Samuel drives home in chapter 7.

**[1 Samuel 4:6-9](/bible/1-samuel/4#v6)**

> <sup>[6](/bible/1-samuel/4#v6)</sup> And when the Philistines heard the noise of the shout, they said, What meaneth the noise of this great shout in the camp of the Hebrews? And they understood that the ark of the Lord was come into the camp.
>
> <sup>[7](/bible/1-samuel/4#v7)</sup> And the Philistines were afraid, for they said, God is come into the camp. And they said, Woe unto us! for there hath not been such a thing heretofore.
>
> <sup>[8](/bible/1-samuel/4#v8)</sup> Woe unto us! who shall deliver us out of the hand of these mighty Gods? these are the Gods that smote the Egyptians with all the plagues in the wilderness.
>
> <sup>[9](/bible/1-samuel/4#v9)</sup> Be strong, and quit yourselves like men, O ye Philistines, that ye be not servants unto the Hebrews, as they have been to you: quit yourselves like men, and fight.

- When the Philistines heard the noise of the shout and understood that the ark of the Lord was come into the camp, they were afraid, saying, God is come into the camp; woe unto us, for there hath not been such a thing heretofore. They had never had to battle Israel with the ark of the covenant in the camp.
- Think on what they said: Who shall deliver us out of the hand of these mighty Gods? These are the Gods that smote the Egyptians with all the plagues. The nations knew what the Most High did to Egypt; it was known throughout the earth, and to this day real history about what the Hebrews and their God did to the Egyptians is still taught on the other side of the earth. With the ark of the commandments among us, the nations understood they were dealing with something above a regular people.
- Everything our people try to glory in about Kemet, the Lord smote down. The ten plagues humiliated ten plus different gods that the Egyptians served, all their power, all their magicians and wizards. Come out of that Kemet movement; the Lord destroyed it and said Egypt would not rise again as a power in the earth.
- Still the Philistines rallied: be strong, and quit yourselves like men, O ye Philistines, that ye be not servants unto the Hebrews, as they have been to you. They remembered serving Israel in the days of the Judges and refused to be slaves again, so they got ready to fight.

  Precepts:
  - **[2 Esdras 1:10](/bible/2-esdras/1#v10)**
    > <sup>[10](/bible/2-esdras/1#v10)</sup> Many kings have I destroyed for their sakes; Pharaoh with his servants and all his power have I smitten down.

    The Most High destroyed many kings for Israel's sake; Pharaoh and all his power is the most popular account, and the Philistines knew it.

**[1 Samuel 4:10-11](/bible/1-samuel/4#v10)**

> <sup>[10](/bible/1-samuel/4#v10)</sup> And the Philistines fought, and Israel was smitten, and they fled every man into his tent: and there was a very great slaughter; for there fell of Israel thirty thousand footmen.
>
> <sup>[11](/bible/1-samuel/4#v11)</sup> And the ark of God was taken; and the two sons of Eli, Hophni and Phinehas, were slain.

- The Philistines fought, Israel was smitten again, and every man fled into his tent; there was a very great slaughter, and thirty thousand footmen of Israel fell. A second loss, far worse than the first, even with the ark in the camp.
- The ark of God was taken, and the two sons of Eli, Hophni and Phinehas, were slain. Those two were wicked as hell, sleeping with the women that assembled at the door of the congregation and finessing the people's offerings, so in this battle the Most High allowed their lives to be taken, exactly as had been prophesied against the house of Eli.

**[1 Samuel 4:12-18](/bible/1-samuel/4#v12)**

> <sup>[12](/bible/1-samuel/4#v12)</sup> And there ran a man of Benjamin out of the army, and came to Shiloh the same day with his clothes rent, and with earth upon his head.
>
> <sup>[13](/bible/1-samuel/4#v13)</sup> And when he came, lo, Eli sat upon a seat by the wayside watching: for his heart trembled for the ark of God. And when the man came into the city, and told it, all the city cried out.
>
> <sup>[14](/bible/1-samuel/4#v14)</sup> And when Eli heard the noise of the crying, he said, What meaneth the noise of this tumult? And the man came in hastily, and told Eli.
>
> <sup>[15](/bible/1-samuel/4#v15)</sup> Now Eli was ninety and eight years old; and his eyes were dim, that he could not see.
>
> <sup>[16](/bible/1-samuel/4#v16)</sup> And the man said unto Eli, I am he that came out of the army, and I fled to day out of the army. And he said, What is there done, my son?
>
> <sup>[17](/bible/1-samuel/4#v17)</sup> And the messenger answered and said, Israel is fled before the Philistines, and there hath been also a great slaughter among the people, and thy two sons also, Hophni and Phinehas, are dead, and the ark of God is taken.
>
> <sup>[18](/bible/1-samuel/4#v18)</sup> And it came to pass, when he made mention of the ark of God, that he fell from off the seat backward by the side of the gate, and his neck brake, and he died: for he was an old man, and heavy. And he had judged Israel forty years.

- A man of Benjamin ran out of the army to Shiloh the same day with his clothes rent and earth upon his head, and found Eli sitting by the wayside watching, for his heart trembled for the ark of God. Eli was very protective of the ark; he did not want anything to happen to it.
- Eli was the high priest who groomed Samuel up, and he was righteous as far as himself, but his sons were devils, and he honoured his sons above the Most High by not rebuking them like a true leader should have.
- Eli was ninety and eight years old and his eyes were dim, and when the messenger told him Israel fled, the slaughter was great, thy two sons are dead, and the ark of God is taken, at the mention of the ark of God he fell from off the seat backward by the side of the gate, and his neck brake, and he died, for he was an old man, and heavy. The shock of the ark being taken is what took him off that seat.
- He had judged Israel forty years, and his death was ultimately part of the judgment for how he dealt with his sons, in that he did not correct them as he should have.

**[1 Samuel 4:19-22](/bible/1-samuel/4#v19)**

> <sup>[19](/bible/1-samuel/4#v19)</sup> And his daughter in law, Phinehas’ wife, was with child, near to be delivered: and when she heard the tidings that the ark of God was taken, and that her father in law and her husband were dead, she bowed herself and travailed; for her pains came upon her.
>
> <sup>[20](/bible/1-samuel/4#v20)</sup> And about the time of her death the women that stood by her said unto her, Fear not; for thou hast born a son. But she answered not, neither did she regard it.
>
> <sup>[21](/bible/1-samuel/4#v21)</sup> And she named the child I–chabod, saying, The glory is departed from Israel: because the ark of God was taken, and because of her father in law and her husband.
>
> <sup>[22](/bible/1-samuel/4#v22)</sup> And she said, The glory is departed from Israel: for the ark of God is taken.

- Phinehas' wife was with child, near to be delivered, and when she heard the tidings that the ark of God was taken and that her father in law and her husband were dead, she bowed herself and travailed, giving birth before her time under all that misfortune.
- Dying, she named the child Ichabod, saying, The glory is departed from Israel: for the ark of God is taken. Remember what the ark contained, the commandments; with the ark gone, she said the glory of Israel was gone. It was a very sad time for the nation of Israel: thirty thousand mighty men lost, Eli dead, and the ark in the hands of the Philistines.
